title: Para-Shooters Allege Selection Fraud, Protest at Asian Para Games Send-Off
excerpt: Akash and Sandeep Kumar questioned their exclusion from the Aichi-Nagoya squad at the Delhi ceremony attended by Sports Minister Mansukh Mandaviya; PCI chief Devendra Jhajharia called the process "100 per cent fair."
body:
• Para-shooters Akash and Sandeep Kumar staged a protest at the Indian contingent's send-off ceremony in New Delhi on Thursday, alleging corruption and score manipulation in the Asian Para Games shooting squad selection.
  • Akash, who says he is Asia's No. 1-ranked para-shooter, and Sandeep, Asia No. 3 in the P4 50m pistol SH1, questioned their exclusion while a shooter they ranked 14th in Asia was selected — and alleged a 20% commission demand on government cash awards.
  • Paralympic Committee of India president Devendra Jhajharia categorically rejected the claims, insisting the selection followed Sports Ministry guidelines with "no discrimination."
  • A Sports Ministry source said genuine grievances would be examined, but the squad is finalised and cannot be changed; the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Para Games open October 18.

The ceremonial send-off of India's Asian Para Games contingent turned confrontational in New Delhi on Thursday, after two para-shooters staged a protest at the event alleging corruption and score manipulation in the shooting squad's selection for the Aichi-Nagoya Games.

The protest at the send-off

Several omitted para-shooters demonstrated at the send-off ceremony, where Union Sports Minister Mansukh Mandaviya was the chief guest and Minister of State for Youth Affairs and Sports Raksha Nikhil Khadse the guest of honour, according to a PTI report. The protesters were led by Akash, a para-shooter who claims he is currently the No. 1-ranked shooter in Asia, and Sandeep Kumar, ranked third in Asia in the P4 50m free pistol SH1 event.

https://x.com/PTI_News/status/2108119738421555315

Their central question was simple: why were they left out while Rudrankksh Khandelwal, whom they said is ranked 14th in Asia, made the squad? Sandeep confronted PCI president Devendra Jhajharia directly at the ceremony. Asked what Jhajharia told him, Sandeep replied: "Nothing."

The allegations

Akash alleged his credentials were overlooked because he had not named shooting coach Jai Prakash Nautiyal as his coach. "That is why he cut my name. I have been here for two months. He keeps saying that we are doing your work," Akash said.

The shooters' allegations went further. They claimed qualifying scores were changed in the national selection trial, that selected athletes lacked comparable international experience — "They (those selected) have not played internationally," the protesters said — and that officials demanded a 20% commission from government cash awards as a condition for selection. They also raised questions about the manipulation of international quota places and the appointment of certain selection officials.

The athletes submitted a representation to the Sports Authority of India seeking an independent inquiry, and warned they could approach the High Court under Article 226 if their grievances were not addressed.

"That is why he cut my name. I have been here for two months. He keeps saying that we are doing your work."

— Akash, para-shooter, on his exclusion from the Asian Para Games squad

The federation's response

The Paralympic Committee of India rejected every allegation. "The selection has been done as per the criteria. There has been no discrimination against anyone. The selections are 100 per cent fair and according to the Sports Ministry's guidelines," Jhajharia told PTI, dismissing Akash's coach-link allegation as "false allegations."

A Sports Ministry source told PTI that genuine grievances would be examined, but added that the Para Asian Games squad is finalised and cannot be changed at this stage.

"The selection has been done as per the criteria. There has been no discrimination against anyone. The selections are 100 per cent fair and according to the Sports Ministry's guidelines."

— Devendra Jhajharia, president, Paralympic Committee of India

What comes next

The protesters' representation to the SAI is now the most likely avenue for redress, with the High Court option held in reserve. But with the Games opening in Nagoya on October 18, any remedy would almost certainly come too late for this squad — the fifth edition of the Asian Para Games runs October 18-24.

The episode lands awkwardly for a system that prides itself on transparency. Mandaviya's own standing position, laid out at the National Sports Federation Conclave on August 7, is that selection trials must be transparent and recorded on camera, and that no athlete should ever face injustice in selection. Whether the SAI inquiry delivers on that standard will be the test.

For the contingent itself, the show goes on. Paralympic champions Pramod Bhagat (para badminton) and Bhavina Patel (para table tennis) will carry the Tricolour as flag bearers at the October 18 opening ceremony. "When you carry the Tricolour, you realise that you are representing something much bigger than yourself," Patel said in the PCI's release.
